checks.finding: design.md:5-17 ('## Architecture Overview') covers all three required elements. (1) Component boundaries: the Stream A/Stream B framing plus the Components table (design.md:19-34) enumerating every touched artifact with status/change. (2) Integration with existing components: explicit statement that 'bootstrap's routing and ship's target selection keep their existing file-based logic exactly (BL-002), and the probe is layered beside it, not in front of it' (design.md:11); the protected-file integration for ship/SKILL.md is handled via the human-copy staging pattern (design.md:24,100), which honours requirements.md:36-40's three task-decomposition constraints: the Components table gives ship/SKILL.md and human-copy/ distinct rows (own-task separability), the Deployment and CI Plan frames Done-when around TEST-025 (staged candidate+manifest) with TEST-026 (live file) expected red rather than blocking (design.md:185, matching requirements.md:39's 'never in terms of the live file's content'), and OQ-007 (design.md:125) flags the human decision explicitly (requirements.md:40's handoff constraint). (3) Technology choices: 'instructional text in a skill, not code... no new script, no new binary' (design.md:9), cross-confirmed by frontend-spec.md:1-9 and infra-spec.md:22-24 ('Nothing is deployed'). Caveat (does not affect this check's verdict, see TEST-STRATEGY-COVERAGE): the Design Decisions section's OQ-005 framing is stale relative to the currently governing requirements.md, but that staleness does not remove any of the three ARCH-COVERAGE elements.

Caveat (does not change verdict): security-spec.md:39's B2 STRIDE row cites only AC-012/AC-013 and predates the AC-027a/AC-027b divergence-reporting addition (see TEST-STRATEGY-COVERAGE finding); REQ-005 itself states the warning 'costs nothing in safety' since AC-012/AC-013 already bind the outcome (requirements.md:146), so the authority-boundary guarantee this check evaluates remains intact.

design.md:132-166 ('## Test Strategy') is substantial (unit/integration/runtime-exercise/regression levels, full per-AC coverage table) but is stale relative to the currently governing requirements.md. requirements.md:144-162 records that OQ-005 (investigation.md:213-214) was resolved by the human on 2026-08-04 to warn-on-divergence, adding live AC-027a and AC-027b (requirements.md:148-156); acceptance-tests.md:38-39 already carries matching TEST-027a/TEST-027b rows. design.md's coverage table (design.md:136-164) has no AC-027a or AC-027b row, and its summary 'Twenty-six live ACs, twenty-seven TEST rows, no AC without a row and no row without an AC' (design.md:166) is now false against the current requirements.md/acceptance-tests.md pair (28 live ACs). Root cause visible in design.md itself: the Design Decisions section still lists OQ-005 in the 'Escalated -- human decision required' table (design.md:117-124) and states 'OQ-005 is the one that should block' (design.md:130), and Risk R-1 (design.md:203) instructs 'task decomposition must not schedule the probe step before it resolves' -- all inheriting investigation.md:213-214's now-superseded framing rather than requirements.md's resolution (requirements.md:160 explicitly: 'investigation.md's OQ-005 entry (:213-214) is superseded by this section and is not to be read as current... accurate when written, wrong now'). Note requirements.md:158 states the divergence behavior definition deliberately 'lands in this specification rather than in design.md' -- so design.md is not expected to restate the warn-on-divergence wording itself -- but that does not excuse the Test Strategy section's own completeness claim, nor the Design Decisions/Risk sections' factual claim that OQ-005 remains open and blocking. Concrete failure mode: a task-decomposer following design.md's Test Strategy table has no instruction to build TEST-027a/TEST-027b coverage, and following R-1's own mitigation text would misread OQ-005 as an unresolved blocker when requirements.md already closed it. Not eligible for [LEGACY COMPAT] downgrade -- the Test Strategy section is fully populated; this is a content-currency defect, not an absent template field.
